findings: The 1-input, 1-output, 1-component case was exactly additive in the split tests.
With 1 input and 4 components, mean component-split MAE remained very small at 0.0000904.
At 32 inputs, 10 outputs and 4 components, mean component-split MAE rose to 0.004305 and input-split MAE to 0.003858.
At 32 inputs, 10 outputs and 8 components, mean component-split MAE rose to 0.008243 and input-split MAE to 0.007869.
Full Q.ANT versus exact-cosine MAE also scaled upward, reaching 0.008776 in the 32x10x8 case.
interpretation: The results are consistent with approximate mathematical additivity plus finite-precision/order-of-accumulation effects that grow with the number of summed terms. They do not establish a fundamental non-additive KAN operation. This also shows that the Exp019 split-call reconstruction itself can introduce error, so its failed reconstruction should not be treated as evidence of non-additive backend semantics.
next_research_direction: Measure full-call Q.ANT-versus-exact-cosine error over a factorial scaling grid of input-channel count and Fourier-component count, without split-call reconstruction, and fit simple scaling models against the total number of accumulated terms.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The experiment did not isolate individual rounding stages inside the backend.
The largest synthetic input dimension was 32, below the 784-dimensional FashionMNIST layer.
